A much smaller and faster model and API image, a browser demo that handles crowds, and the cleanups that came out of the first review.

**Live demo:** https://miguelmochizuki.github.io/fer-2013/

## Changes

- **int8 classifier.** The model is quantized (static QDQ, per-channel weights): 44.7 MB to 11.3 MB, and 3x faster on CPU (5.8 ms versus 17.2 ms for one image). Test accuracy 70.86% versus 70.80%, macro-F1 0.7098 versus 0.7095, ECE after calibration 0.0243 versus 0.0234; 97.5% of predictions equal the fp32 ones. `scripts/quantize_onnx.py` refuses to write a model that drifts from the fp32 one. A first visit to the demo now downloads about 26 MB instead of 59 MB.
- **Docker image: 742 MB to 438 MB** on disk (209 MB to 111 MB compressed). YuNet now runs on ONNX Runtime with the decoding and NMS in numpy, so OpenCV is gone from the image, and the classifier is int8. API p50 is 10 ms (14 ms with the heatmap), down from 23 and 26 ms; on a tenth of a CPU it is 1.3 s instead of 1.8 to 2.0 s, using 94 MiB of memory instead of 212.
- **No cap on the number of faces**, in the API and in the browser (it was 10).
- **Face picker in the demo.** With several faces, a strip of crops (or a click on a box in the photo) selects one reading at a time.
- **Build safety.** The site build refuses an output directory that would delete the sources; the YuNet and onnxruntime licenses ship with the site.
- **Smaller fixes.** A photo dropped during an analysis gets a notice instead of being ignored; the decoded image is freed when an early error happens; dead code removed; the web test names are in English.

## Models

The weights are the [models-v1.2.0](https://github.com/MiguelMochizuki/fer-2013/releases/tag/models-v1.2.0) pre-release (int8, with the fp32 model attached). The browser's probabilities now differ from Python's by up to 3e-3, because int8 kernels round a few activations differently in WebAssembly; the tests allow 1e-2.

## Known limits

- About 71% accuracy on a noisy dataset; emotion labels read off a face are not reliable. Do not use this for decisions about people.
- Small faces in a large crowd photo can be missed, because detection runs on the image downscaled to 640 px.
- PNGs with transparency reach the model as black where alpha is 0.
- The browser demo is checked in Chromium and Firefox. Safari is untested.
